claim: Baiersbronn is the only Black Forest municipality with four certified Genießerpfade (Sankenbachsteig, Satteleisteig, Tonbachsteig, Panoramasteig), each 11-14 km on natural paths through scenic landscape.
quote: zertifizierte Premiumwanderwege ... zwischen 11 und 14 Kilometer lang ... schöne, naturnahe Wege ... Baiersbronner Sankenbachsteig ... Baiersbronner Satteleisteig ... Baiersbronner Tonbachsteig ... Baiersbronner Panoramasteig

claim: The Baiersbronner Wanderhimmel comprises 550 km of marked trails including the four Genießerpfade, nine Himmelswege circular tours, the Seensteig (89.29 km, 5 stages) and the Murgleiter (109.83 km, 5 stages, 3,700 m elevation, rated difficult).
quote: Baiersbronner Wanderhimmel features 550 kilometers of hiking trails with 4 certified Genießerpfade ... Seensteig ... 89.29 km ... Murgleiter ... 109.83 km ... 3,700 meters elevation gain, classified as difficult.

claim: The Sankenbachsteig runs 12.7 km with 430 m elevation gain (approx. 4 hours), passing the Sankenbachsee, a manually-sluiced 40 m Sankenbach waterfall and the Glasmännlehütte at 777 m.
quote: Length: 12.7km ... Elevation Gain: 430m ... Sankenbachsee ... 40-meter Sankenbach waterfall with a manually-operated wooden sluice gate ... Glasmännlehütte mountain hut at 777 meters elevation

claim: The Panoramasteig is a 14.3 km moderate loop with 430 m climb across the 'sun terrace of the Murgtal', featuring the Mähderbrunnen wine fountain (Oberkirch wines cooled in the spring), Blockhaushof picnic spot, and Sackmann's Panorama-Hütte.
quote: 14.3 km ... 430 meters of elevation gain ... past schnapps and wine fountains ... sun terrace of the Murgtal ... Mähderbrunnen Wine Fountain ... bottles of wine ... for tasting cool in the water ... Sackmann's Panorama Hut

claim: The Sankenbachsteig is rated 'very demanding' with 566 m ascent and 522 m descent, starting from the Sesselbahn parking lot in Baiersbronn and passing primordial forest (Bannwald).
quote: Sankenbachsteig ... ca. 13,4 km ... Elevation gain: 566 meters ... Very demanding ... Starting point: Sesselbahn parking lot, Baiersbronn ... urwüchsige Wälder (primordial forests)

claim: The 110 km Murgleiter (5 stages, all rated difficult) is certified by the Deutsches Wanderinstitut as a premium trail, with stage 5 ascending from Baiersbronn 21.7 km to the Schliffkopf.
quote: 110 km long Murgleiter is premium hiking, fulfilling all criteria of the German Hiking Seal (Deutsches Wandersiegel) ... certified by the German Hiking Institute ... Etappe 5: Baiersbronn – Schliffkopf - 21.7 km, difficult

claim: The 14 km Tonbachsteig runs 70% inside the Black Forest National Park with viewpoints at Oberer Zinken and Huzenbacher Seeblick, plus the Kleemisse high moor and the Traube Tonbach log cabin stop.
quote: Old woodmaking trails lead 70% of the way through the Northern Black Forest National Park with magnificent viewpoints at the Oberer Zinken and Huzenbacher Seeblick ... Kleemisse, a high moor area ... Traube Tonbach log cabin

claim: Among the nine Himmelsweg themed loops, the Bannwald-Tour is a hard 13.4 km (8.3 mi) hike with ~624 m (2,047 ft) climb taking 4.5-5 hours along high-moor terrain to Seibelseckle with views to the Rhine plain and Vosges.
quote: Bannwald Tour: This hard hike covers 8.3 miles with an elevation gain of 2,047 feet, and takes about 4.5–5 hours ... high moor level through the Bannwald forest and to the Seibelseckle ... views along the west path to the Rhine plain and the Vosges

claim: Baiersbronn's Bikehimmel offers ~400 km of mountain-bike network with eleven tours from 13-81 km (up to one-third on singletrack); the T6 Hirschkopf-Trailtour is a 35.3 km flagship loop.
quote: 400 kilometers of trail network with eleven varied tours ... 13 to 81 kilometers ... up to one-third of the paths being exciting singletrails ... T6: Hirschkopf-Trailtour ... 35.3 km

claim: Buhlbachsee, a hidden glacial lake in the Obertal forest above Baiersbronn, is a popular short-walk destination reachable from Kniebis, Baiersbronn-Obertal or the Black Forest High Road via gravel and narrow paths.
quote: Buhlbachsee ... reached on foot over various paths including from Kniebis, Baiersbronn-Obertal or from the Black Forest High Road ... hidden and idyllic in the middle of the forest ... gravel and later narrow paths

claim: The Schwarzwaldhochstraße is part of the B500 federal highway running roughly 60 km from Baden-Baden to Freudenstadt at 800–1,000 m elevation, completed in 1952.
quote: leads over 60 km from Baden-Baden to Freudenstadt... at an altitude of between 800 and 1,000 metres above sea level... The entire route from Baden-Baden to Freudenstadt was completed in 1952.

claim: The Mummelsee is the largest of seven remaining cirque lakes in the Black Forest, 3.7 ha, 800 m circumference, 18 m deep, at 1,036 m elevation, named after white water lilies (Mummeln).
quote: Elevation: 1,036 meters... Depth: 18 meters... Size: 3.7 hectares... Circumference: approximately 800 meters... The lake's name derives from white water lilies, locally called Mummeln.

claim: Hornisgrinde (1,164 m) is the highest mountain in the Northern Black Forest, topped by the 23-m Hornisgrinde Tower from 1910 and bordering a 6,000-year-old raised bog up to 5 m thick.
quote: 1,164 m (3,820 ft), is the highest mountain in the Northern Black Forest of Germany... 23-metre-high Hornisgrinde Tower... the raised bog, up to five metres thick... is reckoned to be at least 6,000 years old.

claim: The Lotharpfad is a 900-m boardwalk loop opened in 2003 winding through a 10-ha swath of forest destroyed by Cyclone Lothar on 26 December 1999 (winds to 200 km/h).
quote: approximately 900-meter-long boardwalk loop... 10-hectare area of windthrown forest devastated by the extratropical cyclone Lothar on 26 December 1999... Opened to the public in 2003

claim: The Schliffkopf circular trail is about 3.5 km, ~1.5 hours and 60 m of climb through Grinden heath and old forests with rare species like capercaillie and adders.
quote: approximately 3.5 kilometers... about 1.5 hours to complete, with a modest 60-meter elevation gain... viele seltene Arten wie Auerhühner, Baumpieper, Alpine Gebirgsschrecken oder Kreuzottern

claim: The Schliffkopf summit (1,054 m) along the Schwarzwaldhochstraße has a viewing platform with 360-degree panoramas reaching to the Vosges and Rhine plain on clear days.
quote: Schliffkopf is a 1054m summit along the Schwarzwaldhochstraße that offers a beautiful 360-degree panoramic view... excellent views extending to the Vosges

claim: The Nationalparkzentrum Ruhestein houses a one-way interactive exhibition (~2.5 h) on the rewilding forest, a cinema, the Bridge of Wilderness viewpoint, tourist info shop and café; entry is free.
quote: interactive exhibition on the increasingly wild forest, a cinema, the Bridge of Wilderness, the tourist information centre with a shop for the national park region and a café... one-way exhibition takes about 2.5 hours

claim: The Ruhestein visitor centre is an award-winning architectural landmark whose timber-clad pavilions and 36-m cantilevered Bridge of Wilderness opened in 2021 above the Wildsee cirque.
quote: National Park Center Ruhestein

claim: The Wildnispfad is a guided wilderness trail through Black Forest core zones where deadwood and natural succession are left untouched; ranger-led tours leave from Ruhestein.
quote: Wilderness Trail

claim: From Ruhestein a popular short hike descends to the Wildsee, a small protected cirque lake whose surrounding bann-forest has been left to itself since 1911 and is now part of the national park core zone.
quote: Ruhestein - Lake Wildsee

claim: Freudenstadt was founded in 1599 by Duke Frederick I of Württemberg, designed by architect Heinrich Schickhardt and populated largely by Protestants exiled from Inner Austrian provinces.
quote: Freudenstadt was established in 1599 by Frederick I of Württemberg. The architect Heinrich Schickhardt designed the city, which was populated largely by 11,000 Protestants who left the Inner Austrian provinces.

claim: Freudenstadt's Marktplatz measures 219x216 metres, making it Germany's largest market square; the planned city was designed for 3,500 inhabitants based on a mill board game layout.
quote: The city was designed for 3,500 inhabitants and featured Germany's largest marketplace at 219×216 meters—notably larger than Berlin's population of 6,000 at that time.

claim: The Marktplatz spans 4.74 hectares, is divided into Oberer Marktplatz, Unterer Marktplatz and Postplatz by streets, and features arcaded buildings with 50 water fountains.
quote: The square measures 4.74 hectares and is divided into an Upper Market Square and a Lower Market Square... There are 50 water fountains on the market square, which provide refreshment and are a real crowd-puller, especially in summer.

claim: Freudenstadt's Evangelical Stadtkirche, built 1601-1608 in Gothic/Renaissance style, has a distinctive L-shaped plan occupying a corner of the Marktplatz, allowing segregation of sexes while keeping the whole congregation centered on the preacher.
quote: The L-shaped church in Freudenstadt occupies one corner of the town's main square... pews made possible segregating the sexes, while giving the whole congregation access to the preacher, font, and table, but not to one another.

claim: Panorama-Bad Freudenstadt features a 25-metre sports pool, a 110-metre Black Hole slide, year-round heated outdoor pool, a 1,500 m² vitality area with experience grottos, and a 1,300 m² sauna landscape with five saunas including MeerKlimaSauna.
quote: Black Hole slide: 110 meters long... Vitality area spanning over 1,500 square meters featuring massage jets and experience grottos (salt, fire, ice)... Sauna landscape covering 1,300+ square meters with five different saunas including MeerKlimaSauna and log cabin saunas

claim: Panorama-Bad is one of the most popular regional leisure facilities in northern Black Forest with over 350,000 visitors annually, open Tuesday-Sunday with entry from €5.90 for 105 minutes.
quote: Panorama-Bad is one of the most popular regional leisure facilities in northern Black Forest with over 350,000 visitors annually... Entry starts from €5.90 for 105 minutes.

claim: The Friedrichsturm on the Kienberg, a 25-metre red sandstone observation tower built in 1899 for Freudenstadt's 300th anniversary, is closed November 1 through March 30 for safety reasons and open April to October.
quote: The Friedrichsturm on Freudenstadt's Kienberg is closed during winter for safety reasons, from November 1 through March 30, 2026.

claim: The Kienberg walk from Freudenstadt's marketplace is a short circular hike of about 1.3 km with only ~70 m elevation gain, taking in the Friedrichsturm viewing tower, a café, sunbathing area, water-treading site, rose path and sculptures.
quote: This short circular route takes you up Freudenstadt's local peak, the Kienberg, with its viewing tower, café, sunbathing area, water-treading site, rose path and various sculptures. From the marketplace, you overcome approximately 1.3 km and about 70 meters in elevation.

claim: The Sankenbach waterfall southwest of Baiersbronn drops more than 40 metres in several stages over the Karwand of the Sankenbachkessel; the flow is triggered by manually opening a wooden sluice.
quote: The Sankenbach waterfalls are located southwest of Baiersbronn in the Black Forest, with the Sankenbach crashing in several stages more than 40 meters over the Karwand of the Sankenbachkessel... The Sankenbach waterfall is triggered by manually opening the wooden sluice

claim: The Murgtalbahn is a 58.2 km railway connecting Rastatt and Freudenstadt; the Royal Württemberg State Railways began service to Klosterreichenbach on 20 November 1901, and steam locomotives were replaced by diesel in 1966.
quote: the Royal Württemberg State Railways started operations to Klosterreichenbach on 20 November 1901... In 1966 steam locomotives on the Murg Valley Railway were replaced by diesel locomotives.

claim: Historic steam train trips along the Murgtalbahn run from Karlsruhe through Rastatt, Gernsbach, Weisenbach and Klosterreichenbach to Baiersbronn, with catering and free bicycle transport; 2026 bookings opened 31 March 2026.
quote: Bookings for 2026 Murgtalbahn steam train rides are available from March 31, 2026... continues past Schloss Eberstein toward Hilpertsau, and from Weisenbach onwards features numerous bridges and tunnels before passing through Klosterreichenbach to reach the spa town of Baiersbronn.

claim: Bad Wildbad's Sommerberg (within ~30 km) features a 1,250 m treetop walk up to 20 m high and the WILDLINE suspension bridge, 380 m long and up to 60 m above the Enz valley.
quote: The Bad Wildbad Treetop Walk is 1,250 meters long and floats up to 20 meters above the forest floor... The WILDLINE suspension bridge is 380 meters long and stretches over the Enz Valley at a height of up to 60 meters.

claim: Baiersbronn's ice rink, measuring 30x45 metres, is described as unique within a 60 km radius and rents skates from its ticket office.
quote: an ice rink in nearby Baiersbronn measures 30 x 45 metres and is unique within a radius of 60 kilometres, with skates available for hire at the ticket office.

claim: Kloster Allerheiligen was a Premonstratensian monastery near Oppenau founded with a charter issued by Duchess Uta of Schauenburg in 1196, located at 620 m elevation in the upper Lierbach valley.
quote: All Saints' Abbey was a Premonstratensian monastery near Oppenau in the Black Forest. ... In 1196, the foundation charter was issued by Duchess Uta. ... It is located at 620 metres above sea level in the upper valley of the Lierbach

claim: The founding legend dates a wooden chapel built around 1192 by Uta of Schauenburg; statues of Saint Helena, Uta of Schauenburg and Gerung from the abbey survive above the Lichtenthal Abbey prince's chapel gateway.
quote: All Saints' Abbey (Kloster Allerheiligen) was a Premonstratensian monastery founded around 1192 when a wooden chapel was built ... Three statues from All Saints' Abbey are above the gateway of the prince's chapel at Lichtenthal Abbey, representing Saint Helena, Uta of Schauenburg and Gerung.

claim: The Allerheiligen waterfalls plunge almost 90 metres across seven cascades, accessed by a picturesque gorge path opened in 1840 with numerous stairways and several bridges.
quote: over seven cascades plunge almost 90 metres down the steep rocks ... path that leads visitors along the gorge via numerous stairways and over several bridges ... opened up in 1840 ... In 1842 they provided a total of 100 guilders to create a broader and safer pathway for the general public. Stairs replaced the ladders

claim: The waterfalls reach roughly 100 metres in total drop across seven cascades (the main section measured at 83 m) and are considered the Black Forest's largest natural waterfall, with free parking at the Lierbachtal valley site (620 m).
quote: 83 Meter tief ... sieben Kaskaden ... gut 100 Meter ... Kostenfreie Parkplätze zum Parken sind vorhanden ... der größten natürlichen Wasserfalls des Schwarzwaldes

claim: The Komoot Allerheiligen Waterfalls–Abbey ruins loop from Oppenau is 13.2 km with 370 m of elevation gain and about 3 h 53 min duration, rated moderate, starting from the Sohlberg area parking.
quote: Loop Length: 13.2km ... Duration: 03:53 ... Difficulty: Moderate ... Elevation Gain: 370m ... The starting point is located at a parking lot in the Sohlberg area.

claim: The Sohlberg-Blick viewpoint sits at 1,002 m on the Oppenau–Melkereikopf–Schliffkopf–Allerheiligen circuit, between Hermann-Beier-Hütte and Melkereikopf along a 15.58 km route with 681 m of elevation gain.
quote: Sohlberg-Blick viewpoint sits at "1.002 m" elevation and is located "6,5 km" along the route ... overall tour spans 15.58 km with 681 meters of elevation gain ... between the Hermann-Beier-Hütte (5.9 km mark) and Melkereikopf summit (6.7 km mark)

claim: The Allerheiligen Wasserfälle are listed by Baiersbronn tourism as a regional excursion destination reached via the B500 Schwarzwaldhochstraße and Ruhestein pass into the Lierbach valley toward Oppenau.
quote: Allerheiligen Wasserfälle

claim: Restaurant Kloster Allerheiligen sits directly adjacent to the ruins at Allerheiligen 6, 77728 Oppenau, serving regional Slow-Food-listed cuisine with Mangalitza pork and produce from Demeter farms.
quote: Restaurant Kloster Allerheiligen ... Allerheiligen 6, 77728 Oppenau ... meat from Mangalitza heritage pigs ... recommended in the Slow Food dining guide ... homemade dishes and products from local Demeter farms

claim: Other Oppenau-area viewpoints include the 28-metre Buchkopfturm (opened April 2015, ~900 m elevation) and the 1890 Moosturm on the Mooskopf, complementing the Sohlbergblick on the Allerheiligen circuits.
quote: Buchkopfturm Oppenau, opened in April 2015 ... 28 meters high and is located at approximately 900 meters above sea level ... Moosturm observation tower has stood since 1890

claim: Kloster Alpirsbach opens Apr 1–Nov 1 Wed–Sat 10:30–16:00 and Sun/holidays 11:00–16:30; off-season Sat/Sun/holidays 11:00–15:00; adult admission €8 standard or €10 with guided tour.
quote: Wed., Thu., Fri., Sat. 10:30 am - 04:00 pm ... Sun., Holiday 11:00 am - 04:30 pm ... Sat., Sun., Holiday 11:00 am - 03:00 pm

claim: Alpirsbach Abbey was founded in 1095 by three noblemen donating ~50 km² to the Benedictine order; its Romanesque church dedicated to St Nicholas was consecrated in 1128 and built 1125–1133, following the Hirsau Reform.
quote: donated about 50 square kilometers (19 mi2) of property to the Order of Saint Benedict ... Romanesque style ... abbey church, dedicated to Saint Nicholas, was consecrated in 1128

claim: The museum's permanent exhibit 'Monks and Scholars' occupies the former abbot's quarters and showcases shoes, doublets, schoolboy homework, drawings and report cards preserved in the cloister's hollow vault spaces.
quote: Letters, homework and drawings done by students ... Shoes, shirts, men's pants, and doublets ... hollow spaces in the severies of the east cloister wing

claim: The Alpirsbacher Kreuzgangkonzerte have run since 1952 in the Gothic cloister courtyard; the 2026 summer season features four Saturday-evening concerts on 27 June, 11 July, 25 July and 1 August, each at 20:00.
quote: Kreuzgangkonzerte ... seit 1952 ... Saturday, June 27, 2026 at 8:00 PM – Friedemann Wuttke ... August 1, 2026 – Arcis Saxophone Quartet

claim: Alpirsbacher Klosterbräu runs daily public Brauwelt tours at 12:00 and 14:30 lasting about 90 minutes, covering the historic Sudhaus and brewing process with one freshly tapped beer included in standard admission.
quote: Daily tours at 12:00 and 14:30 ... Approximately 90 minutes per tour ... One fresh-tapped draft beer included with standard admission

claim: The Brauwelt complex extends beyond the museum to include a wedding chapel in the former brewhouse, a beer cellar, monastery distillery, an on-site beer-praline confectionery and a glass-blowing workshop, plus the Brauladen retail shop.
quote: Original Alpirsbacher beer mugs, vintage advertising signs, fan apparel, and specialty beer mustard ... on-site confectionery producing handmade beer pralines and a glass-blowing workshop

claim: Alpirsbacher Spezial — the brewery's flagship 'kraftvolles Klosterbier' — is a full-bodied Helles-style lager with a brilliant golden colour, fine-pored foam and floral-fruity hop aroma over malt.
quote: kraftvolles Klosterbier with a round, full-bodied character ... brilliant golden coloring with fine-pored foam and aromas of malt mixed with floral-fruity hop notes

claim: Alpirsbacher Pils is a 4.9% ABV bright golden-yellow Pilsner brewed with selected aroma hops and brewing barley, delivering the typical fine-herbal Pils character.
quote: bright golden-yellow color and its typical fine-herbal taste – thanks to finest aroma hops and selected brewing barley ... 4.9%

claim: Kloster Helles is a 5.1% ABV malt-aromatic full beer brewed with Black Forest brewing water, two-row summer-barley malt, 100% natural hops and the brewery's own monastery yeast.
quote: famous Black Forest brewing water, malt from two-row summer barley, 100% natural hops, and Alpirsbacher monastery yeast, with an alcohol content of 5.1% by volume

claim: Bad Wildbad is approximately 38.5 km by road from Baiersbronn with a 39-minute drive, beyond the strict 30 km radius.
quote: The road distance is 38.5 km and takes approximately 39 minutes. This is the fastest and cheapest option, costing €5–8.

claim: The Sommerbergbahn funicular opened in 1908, is 756 m long, climbs 324 m at up to 53% gradient, and takes about 3.5 minutes from Bad Wildbad town to the Sommerberg plateau.
quote: Length: 756 metres (2,480 ft); Elevation gain: 324 metres (1,063 ft); Gradient: 53%; Ride Duration: approximately 3.5 minutes; opened in 1908

claim: The Baumwipfelpfad Schwarzwald features a 40-metre observation tower on the Sommerberg, with a 55-metre tunnel slide inside and a barrier-free, wheelchair-accessible walkway.
quote: 40-metre-high observation tower ... Features a 55-metre tunnel slide inside ... The Treetop Walk and the lookout tower do not have any steps at all and are thus fully accessible for wheelchairs, walkers and prams

claim: The treetop walk is 1,250 metres long, runs up to 20 metres above the forest floor through beech, fir and spruce, and offers a 360° panorama from its 40 m tower.
quote: The path has a total length of 1,250 metres and winds through beech, fir and spruce trees at heights of up to 20 metres above the forest floor

claim: The Wildline suspension bridge opened in July 2018, spans 380 m suspended from two steel cables in a unique arched form, and rises about 60 m above the Enz valley.
quote: The new suspension bridge opened in July 2018 ... built in the form of an arch and is the only suspension bridge of its kind in Europe. The suspension is realized through 2 steel cables ... over a length of 380 meters

claim: Wildline operates daily 9:00–19:30 (last entry 19:00) at Heermannsweg 100 on the Sommerberg in Bad Wildbad.
quote: täglich geöffnet 9-19:30 Uhr, letzter Einlass 19 Uhr ... Heermannsweg 100 in Bad Wildbad

claim: Palais Thermal was completed in 1847 as the Graf-Eberhard-Bad, designed by Nikolaus Friedrich von Thouret, with bathing tradition documented back to 1521 and a full restoration reopening in December 1995.
quote: Completed in 1847, originally named 'Graf-Eberhard-Bad' ... Architect: Nikolaus Friedrich von Thouret ... centuries-old bathing tradition documented since 1521 ... reopened in December 1995 as 'Palais Thermal'

claim: Palais Thermal operates as a textile-optional bath: pools may be used with or without swimwear, but saunas and upper floors are textile-free (nude); Tuesdays are designated textile days when swimwear is allowed throughout.
quote: All pools may be used either with or without swimwear – in the saunas, removing swimwear is mandatory ... the upper floors, including the saunas and rooftop pool, are textile-free (nude). Tuesdays are the designated textile day

claim: The spa houses 12 thermal pools at 32–38 °C across 2,000 m² on four levels, including Moorish halls with 1.4 million mosaic tiles and a panoramic outdoor sun-deck pool.
quote: 12 thermal pools at 32 to 38 degrees Celsius ... 2,000 square metres across four levels ... interior Moorish Hall features 1.4 million mosaic tiles

claim: The Enztalradweg is a signposted 100+ km cycle path running from the Enz source near Enzklösterle through Bad Wildbad and Pforzheim to the Neckar at Walheim, mostly downhill and easy.
quote: The continuously signposted cycling route, over 100 km long, leads from the Enz source in the Black Forest near Enzklösterle to the Enz mouth in the lovely Neckar valley in the wine town of Walheim ... The entire cycle path is mostly downhill

claim: Bad Wildbad sits on the Enztalradweg between Enzklösterle and Höfen an der Enz, making it a natural day-trip cycling base for the Northern Black Forest section.
quote: Bad Wildbad ... Enztalradweg

claim: Bad Wildbad's Kurpark and adjacent Enzauenpark, opened for the 1992 State Garden Show, span ~38 acres along the Enz with water playgrounds, the Römerauen game park and a riverside bike path.
quote: Enzauenpark has been a popular recreation and amusement park for families since the State Garden Show in 1992. The 38-acre Enzauenpark

claim: Bad Herrenalb sits about 47.5 km and 56 minutes by car from Baiersbronn, well outside a 30 km day-trip radius.
quote: The road distance is 47.5 km. It takes approximately 56 min to drive from Baiersbronn to Bad Herrenalb.

claim: Bad Herrenalb is a small Black Forest spa town 30 km south of Karlsruhe centred on the Siebentäler Therme thermal baths, a Kurpark, and hiking such as the 15.5 km Teufelsmühle trail.
quote: Bad Herrenalb is a small spa town located in the Black Forest, 30 km south of Karlsruhe ... The Siebentäler or Seven Valleys Therme ... A 15.5 km hike to the Teufelsmühle

claim: Naturbad Mitteltal in Baiersbronn-Mitteltal opens for the 2026 season on 14 May 2026 with biologically treated water, a 25m basin, diving rock, toddler pool with slide, massage jets and playground.
quote: 25-meter swimming basin; Jump rock with diving board; Shallow area for non-swimmers with sun loungers, massage jets, and water features; Toddler pool with slide and tunnel; open for the 2026 season starting May 14th

claim: Naturbad Mitteltal entry prices are €5 adults, €3 children 6-14, free under 6, with weekday hours 12-20 (10-20 on weekends/holidays).
quote: Adults: €5.00; Children (6-14 years): €3.00; Under 6: Free admission; Evening ticket (from 5 PM): €3.00; Weekdays during school: noon–8 PM; Weekends/holidays/school breaks: 10 AM–8 PM

claim: The Wildgehege Ellbachtal in Mitteltal (Ellbachstrasse, 72270 Baiersbronn) lets visitors see red deer up close and has a playground directly next to the enclosure.
quote: you may encounter the stag and his herd quite nearby; A playground is located directly adjacent to the wildlife enclosure

claim: Baiersbronn maintains five free wildlife enclosures across its districts — Sankenbachtal, Mitteltal (Eulengrund, Ellbachtal), Tonbach, Klosterreichenbach (Ailwald) and Hinterlangenbach — showing red and fallow deer.
quote: There are game reserves in the districts of Baiersbronn (Sankenbachtal), Mitteltal (Eulengrund and Ellbachtal), Tonbach, Klosterreichenbach (Ailwald) and Hinterlangenbach

claim: The Alternativer Wolf- und Bärenpark Schwarzwald at Bad Rippoldsau-Schapbach opens daily 10-18 (March-October), charging €14 adults / €12 reduced / €35 family ticket.
quote: March–October: 10 AM–6 PM; Adults: €14; Reduced (students, seniors, disabled, children 5-14): €12; Family (2 adults + max 2 children): €35

claim: The Bad Rippoldsau Wolf and Bear Park houses 10 brown bears, 3 wolves and lynx rescued from poor captivity on 10 hectares of forest and meadow, with a natural playground and explorer trail.
quote: Ten brown bears and three wolves currently live in the idyllic Wolftal; On 10 hectares of forest and meadow, visitors can watch these animals and also enjoy a natural playground, an exciting explorer trail

claim: Baiersbronn has four minigolf venues spread across the valleys — central Baiersbronn (Sankenbachstr. 12), Obertal (Buhlbachsaue 15), Klosterreichenbach (Naturerlebnis with natural obstacles) and Schönmünzach (Murgtalstr. 622).
quote: Sankenbachstraße 12, 72270 Baiersbronn; Buhlbachsaue 15, 72270 Baiersbronn; Minigolf Naturerlebnis Klosterreichenbach; Murgtalstr. 622

claim: Adventure Golf Freudenstadt (Karl-von-Hahn-Str. 132, ~7km from Baiersbronn) offers 18 themed courses with Black Forest landmarks, costing €10 adults / €8.50 kids 6-15 / €5 under 5.
quote: Adults/teens (16+): €10.00 per round; Children/teens (6-15 years): €8.50 per round; Young children (up to 5 years): €5.00 per round; 18 individualized courses

claim: Experimenta Freudenstadt is a hands-on science Mitmachmuseum with five experiment categories (Air & Water, Waves & Sound, Light & Shadow, Force & Mass, Magnetism) at Musbacher Str. 5.
quote: Air & Water; Waves & Sound; Light & Shadow; Force & Mass; Magnetism; recommended for every age; Musbacher Straße 5, 72250 Freudenstadt

claim: Experimenta Freudenstadt admission is €8 adults, €6 children up to 17, €25 family card for 2 adults + 2 children, with under-3s free.
quote: Children up to 3 years: free entry; Children up to 17 years: €6.00; Adults: €8.00; Family card for 2 adults + 2 children: €25.00

claim: Hauffs Märchen-Museum in Baiersbronn-Klosterreichenbach (Alte Reichenbacher Str. 1) opens Wed/Sat/Sun 14-17 with a children's activity area for playing, painting and crafting, admission €1.50.
quote: Adults pay €1.50. With a Baiersbronner guest card, admission is €1.00; open Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday from 14:00-17:00; children's activity area for playing, painting and crafting

claim: Freudenstadt's Museum im Stadthaus offers free admission across five levels covering Black Forest tourism history, rafting, mining and forestry, open Tue-Sun 10-17.
quote: free admission; five levels; Der Wald lockt; spa culture, grand hotels, fresh air; Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00

claim: The Forellenhof Buhlbach trout farm in the Buhlbachtal raises ~65,000 rainbow trout, salmon trout, golden trout and char annually for its restaurant, sited at the edge of the national park.
quote: Rainbow trout, salmon trout, golden trout and char are raised here, producing about 65,000 food fish per year; idyllic nature conservation area at the edge of the national park
